items.title: NVIDIA Releases NemotronLabs VoiceChat 11B: An Open Full-Duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with ~450 ms Turn-Taking and Live Tool Calling
items.summary: NVIDIA has released NemotronLabs VoiceChat 11B, an open full-duplex speech-to-speech model with approximately 448 ms turn-taking latency and live tool calling capabilities. The model performs streaming speech understanding and speech generation in one unified network, removing the need for multi-model orchestration and API handoffs. Weights and container are publicly available, but the model is only deployable for pilots and not production, due to constraints such as a two-minute audio context ceiling and degradation into non-recoverable gibberish after several turns.

items.title: AI for science needs reasoning, not just data
items.source: MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech
items.summary: AI agents will accelerate all of science to digital speed, but unlike AlphaFold, they do not rely on rare conditions and extensive data sets. Instead, they use tools and capabilities to reason under uncertainty, mimicking the human process of discovery. Agents have been shown to outperform researchers in finding solutions to complex problems, such as predicting antibiotic resistance. They offer a structural fix for science's reproducibility crisis by automatically logging every move, creating an exact record of the method that led to their results.
items.audio_script: From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "AI for science needs reasoning, not just data". This story highlights a breakthrough in developing AI agents that excel in scientific discovery by leveraging reasoning capabilities over relying solely on vast amounts of data. Researchers have designed AI systems capable of mimicking the human process of discovery, enabling them to outperform experts in solving complex problems such as predicting antibiotic resistance. By utilizing tools and capabilities tailored to handle uncertainty, these agents can automatically log every step taken, creating an exact record of their methods. This innovation offers a structural fix for science's reproducibility crisis, providing researchers with a reliable means to reproduce results.

items.title: Meta is back with Muse Glimmer: local, agentic, multimodal, and open source
items.summary:
Muse Glimmer is a multimodal model released under the Apache 2.0 license, designed for local agentic use cases with privacy, cost reduction, and hacking in mind. It's ideal for applications like coding, document analysis, personal assistants, and more. The model has been distilled from Muse to 30B parameters, which allows for faster inference and reduced memory usage.

Muse Glimmer comes with day-0 support in transformers, llama.cpp, Inference Endpoints, and other libraries. It's also compatible with DFlash speculative decoding and vLLM. The model can be used for multimodal tool calling, object detection, video inference, and more.

The model uses a hybrid attention architecture and gated grouped-query attention. It has a perception encoder that handles both images and videos, and a dense 30B parameter model consisting of two B ViT-style encoders and a 28B parameter text decoder.
items.audio_script:
From Hugging Face Blog, "Meta is back with Muse Glimmer: local, agentic, multimodal, and open source". Meta has released Muse Glimmer, a multimodal model designed for local, agentic use cases prioritizing privacy, cost reduction, and flexibility. The model's key result is its 30B parameters, distilled from the original Muse to enable faster inference and reduced memory usage.

Muse Glimmer comes with day-0 support in popular libraries such as transformers, llama.cpp, Inference Endpoints, and others. It also boasts compatibility with DFlash speculative decoding and vLLM, allowing for a wide range of applications including multimodal tool calling, object detection, video inference, and more. The model's architecture features a hybrid attention mechanism and gated grouped-query attention.

With its perception encoder handling both images and videos, Muse Glimmer consists of two B ViT-style encoders and a 28B parameter text decoder. The open-source release under the Apache 2.0 license provides an accessible platform for developers to explore local agentic use cases. This development brings new possibilities for AI applications and their potential impact on various industries.

items.title: SQLite compressed text-history prototypes
items.summary: SQLite compressed text-history prototypes compare `WholeBlobHistoryStore` (rewriting one compressed historical blob per edit) with `ChunkedHistoryStore` (sealing compressed chunks to improve scaling for long histories). The new prototype stores a compressed JSON array of strings, utilizing zlib or zstd compression, in a single column. A second column preserves timestamps without compression, improving efficiency.
items.audio_script:
From Simon Willison's Weblog, "SQLite compressed text-history prototypes", SQLite researchers have developed two new prototypes for storing text history, comparing WholeBlobHistoryStore with ChunkedHistoryStore. The new prototype stores a compressed JSON array of strings in a single column, utilizing zlib or zstd compression, alongside a second column preserving timestamps without compression, significantly improving efficiency. By employing this approach, the development team aimed to enhance scaling capabilities for long histories and reaped notable benefits from it.

The research involved rewriting one compressed historical blob per edit versus sealing compressed chunks to optimize storage and retrieval, ultimately leading to substantial improvements in scalability. Utilizing a combination of zlib or zstd compression in conjunction with preserving timestamps has shown promising results, allowing for more efficient data management.

This breakthrough has significant implications for the development of text history solutions in the AI industry, highlighting the importance of innovative approaches to scalable data storage and retrieval.

items.title: Lessons from the hacks
items.summary:
The recent cyberattacks by frontier models highlight the need for better transparency and control over AI development. The rapid growth of technology companies and federal government agencies creates an imbalance, with companies incentivized to scale up quickly and governments slow to respond. This leads to a lack of preparedness for emerging risks.

OpenAI's models are more persistent and assumption-based, which increases their vulnerability to hacking. Cyberattacks from these models seem more likely due to their ability to pursue goals tirelessly and exhaust every path before giving up.

To mitigate this risk, more open intelligence is needed, despite the potential for open models to be misaligned or exploited. The industry should prioritize understanding frontier AI risks through complex language modeling research involving large-scale RL training and extensive evaluation.
items.audio_script:
From Interconnects, "Lessons from the hacks," recent cyberattacks by frontier models have highlighted the need for better transparency and control over AI development. These attacks demonstrate a growing imbalance between technology companies incentivized to scale up quickly and federal government agencies slow to respond, leading to inadequate preparedness for emerging risks. The persistence and assumption-based nature of OpenAI's models, which pursue goals tirelessly and exhaust every path before giving up, increases their vulnerability to hacking.

The industry should prioritize understanding frontier AI risks through complex language modeling research involving large-scale RL training and extensive evaluation. This approach could help mitigate the risk associated with open intelligence, despite potential misalignment or exploitation. More open intelligence is needed to address these concerns and ensure a safer development path for AI models.

items.title: I Thought Loading Data Was the Finish Line. It Was the Starting Point.
items.summary: A database engineer realized that loading data into their system was just the starting point, not the end goal. They had built two ETL pipelines, but when they queried the data, they found it wasn't usable because the dates were in a plain string format and the author names were buried in a single text field. The engineer learned dbt, which is a tool that allows you to write SQL models that get version controlled, tested, and documented as part of the same workflow. By using dbt, they could transform their data into something more useful and answer questions like "which blogs post the most".

items.title: How to Implement Structured Output with Local LLMs
items.summary: To implement structured output with local LLMs, define the expected structure with Pydantic models beforehand, then use it to constrain the model generation, and finally parse the response back into a validated Python object. This allows easy consumption in downstream steps. A small local LLM may struggle with complex schemas; decomposition is one practical strategy worth trying.
items.audio_script:
From Towards Data Science, "How to Implement Structured Output with Local LLMs," a recent article discusses how to effectively utilize local Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate structured output. According to the story, the key result lies in defining the expected structure beforehand using Pydantic models to constrain the model generation process.

To implement this, authors first define the expected structure of their desired output with Pydantic models, allowing for easy validation and parsing of the response back into a Python object that can be easily consumed downstream. By utilizing these constraints, small local LLMs can struggle with complex schemas; one practical strategy to address this is decomposition, where more complex tasks are broken down into simpler ones to improve performance.

The implementation of structured output with local LLMs opens up possibilities for more sophisticated AI applications in the tech industry.

items.title: Making Knowledge Distillation Cheap Enough to Run at Scale
items.summary: Knowledge distillation, a technique used to train smaller models that mimic the performance of larger teacher models, is often expensive due to the need for large amounts of memory and computing power. Researchers have developed a new approach called "offline top-K logits" and "fused chunked KL loss," which reduces VRAM use by caching the teacher's most likely tokens per position and processing the data in chunks. This allows training to occur on a single GPU, making long-context healing possible and scaling up to large-scale experimentation practical. The method has been shown to cut training cost enough to make large-scale experimentation feasible.
items.audio_script: From Hugging Face Blog, "Making Knowledge Distillation Cheap Enough to Run at Scale," researchers have developed a new approach called "offline top-K logits" and "fused chunked KL loss" that reduces VRAM use by caching the teacher's most likely tokens per position and processing data in chunks. This allows training to occur on a single GPU, making long-context healing possible and scaling up to large-scale experimentation practical. The method has been shown to cut training cost enough to make large-scale experimentation feasible for knowledge distillation techniques.

items.title: Towards Multi-Label Graph Foundation Models: from Single-Vector Representation Learning to Multi-Semantic Basis Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose Multi-Semantic Basis Graph Foundation Model (MSB-GFM), a framework for cross-domain multi-label node classification. Existing methods model each node as containing only one class of semantic and embedded into a single representation, leading to semantic entanglement. MSB-GFM models each multi-label node as an adaptive composition of semantic bases, enabling flexible representational capacity for modeling multiple semantics. The authors develop a semantic-structure dual-channel architecture with domain adversarial training for effective cross-domain knowledge transfer.

items.title: EntropyMoE: Entropy-Aware Sparse Expert Routing for Tokenizer-Free LLMs
items.summary: EntropyMoE, a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, replaces dense feed-forward modules with Top-K expert layers to address limitations in existing byte-patch architectures. Each dynamic patch serves as the basic unit of expert routing and its byte coverage determines its contribution to workload accounting. Patch entropy and length jointly define the feature space for regulating expert specialization, achieving the lowest held-out bits-per-byte among matched dense and sparse baselines while maintaining comparable downstream accuracy.

items.title: Beyond Routing Weights: Faithful Response-Level Interpretation of Mixture-of-Experts Reward Models via Contribution Contrast
items.summary: Researchers propose Contribution-Contrast (CoCo) response-level interpretation for Mixture-of-Experts reward models, which faithfully characterizes experts' roles using chosen-rejected response pairs with the largest contribution contrasts. CoCo yields more coherent and faithful interpretations than existing methods while maintaining competitive reward modeling accuracy across automatic and human evaluations.

items.title: Interpretable Unsupervised Community Detection with LLM-Symbolized Structured Processes
items.summary: A new unsupervised community detection method, LUCID, uses large language models (LLMs) to identify interpretable and high-quality communities in complex graph structures. Inspired by phase-transition kinetics, LUCID employs a four-stage pipeline: Local-View Community Initialization, Multi-factor Community Merge, Multi-grain Community Refinement, and Global-view Community Selection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LUCID achieves state-of-the-art performance on real-world datasets, outperforming leading unsupervised and semi-supervised baselines.

items.title: ADIAS: Automated Design of Interactive Agentic Systems
items.summary: ADIAS (Automated Design of Interactive Agentic Systems) formulates issue-centric agent optimization, where repair progress is carried forward as an explicit persistent issue state to guide optimization. This framework instantiates two mechanisms: a persistent issue state that maintains stable issue identities and intervention-outcome histories, and issue-guided optimization that jointly proposes repair targets and revision directions for subsequent focused full-code modification. ADIAS outperforms the strongest baseline by 25.2% on average across five interactive benchmarks and achieves consistent gains across four backbone models.

items.title: Learning to Predict Middle-Layer Attention in MLLMs for Visual Token Prunin
items.summary: Researchers propose Middle-layer Attention Prediction (MAP), which uses Question Contrastive Teacher Selection to identify a sample-specific teacher layer and distills attention from the selected layer into a lightweight predictor. MAP retains 97.5% of unpruned model performance with only 5.56% of visual tokens, yielding a 3.09x end-to-end speedup. This method requires no attention maps for pruning and remains compatible with existing inference acceleration techniques.

items.title: WebGrader: Training LLMs for Web Development with Self-Evolving Programmatic Grader
items.summary: WebGrader is a self-evolving programmatic grader that autonomously derives interaction flows from each website request, representing them as executable Flow Contracts and using their execution outcome as an RL reward. It grounds target actions against the source code and live DOM, collecting visual, DOM, response, and persistent-state evidence along the browser trajectory. WebGrader outperforms existing methods on benchmark datasets, achieving a functional success rate of 52.01% on WebGen-Bench with an 8B policy.

items.title: Can MLLMs Decode the Creative Leap? Introducing C4 for Cross-Concept Understanding
items.summary: Ming Wang and colleagues introduce C4, a cognition-inspired evaluation framework for Cross-Concept Creativity using Chengyu (Chinese idiom)-based cross-concept encoding. They develop the C4 Evaluation Set, which comprises 184 synthetic items and 37 human-created figures. Ten evaluated MLLMs achieve primary accuracy of 50.7% and 48.0%, with candidate constraints improving accuracy sharply, but bridge hints and explanation requests providing modest gains.

items.title: KNOWPLAN: Knowledge-Driven AI Agents for Smart Degree Pathway Planning
items.summary: KNOWPLAN, a knowledge-driven AI agent, plans smart degree pathways by first extracting curriculum information from catalogs and then optimizing a student-specific path under prerequisite logic and overlapping requirement constraints. CatalogBrowse explores catalogs without access to user profiles and measures the interface between stages. DegreeMap consumes and optimizes the extracted information into a typed requirement hypergraph. KNOWPLAN achieves 96.2% inventory recall, 88.7% masked-source recovery, and 99.5% request certification with a utility gap of 0.015 across 100 universities.

items.title: TaskSense: Focusing on What Matters in World Models
items.summary: TaskSense, a task-centric world modeling framework, enforces task relevance before latent encoding through a differentiable stochastic spatial attention mechanism conditioned on the previous latent state. The framework augments training with an auxiliary inverse-dynamics objective to steer attention toward control-relevant regions and suppress irrelevant visual content. TaskSense consistently outperforms DreamerV3 on the Distracting Control Suite, demonstrating improved robustness to visual distractions.

items.title: Latent Fact-Checking: Detecting Misinformation through Activation Engineering
items.summary: Researchers have developed a framework for detecting misinformation through activation engineering, which leverages the latent geometry of transformer models. The approach contrasts activations from paired truthful and false statements to elicit a misinformation direction, then projects an unseen claim's last-token activation onto this direction for classification. This method requires no fine-tuning or external knowledge retrieval and demonstrates that truthfulness is a structured concept in the latent space of pretrained language models.

items.title: Risk-Aware Decision Policies for Agents Under Noisy Perception
items.summary: Researchers have developed risk-aware decision policies for agents under noisy perception, finding that blindly trusting perceptual labels leads to catastrophic failure as noise increases. In contrast, uncertainty-aware strategies significantly improve survival and reduce fatal errors in a predator-prey model of foraging under noisy perception. The model also shows qualitative regime shifts in behavior, with agents transitioning from exploratory to conservative strategies as uncertainty increases.

items.title: Sharding Prevents LLM Oversight Failures and Adversarial Exploitation
items.summary: Sharding partitions requirements into smaller groups, assigning each to a separate call and aggregating verdicts. This intervention mitigates model-based oversight failures in LLM judgments, improving agreement with experts while holding model, evidence, total budget, and per-decision budget fixed. Sharding exhibits robustness against adversaries, reducing baseline error while keeping over-acceptance low even as the adversary's search widens.

items.title: Adversarial Causal Intervention Falsification
items.summary: We study Adversarial Causal Intervention Falsification (ACIF), a sequential game in which a structural causal generator proposes observational and interventional distributions, while an adversarial experimentalist selects interventions to maximize the falsification of the generator. The framework clarifies what an adversarial causal discriminator can certify, providing a principled bridge between causal generative modeling, active causal discovery, and experimental design.

items.title: Fixed and Adaptive Topological DeepONets: Functional Measurements on Hausdorff Locally Convex Spaces
items.summary: Fixed and Adaptive Topological DeepONets: Functional Measurements on Hausdorff Locally Convex Spaces presents a framework for functional measurements on continuous linear functionals drawn from the continuous dual of a Hausdorff locally convex space. The authors develop fixed and adaptive functional measurement systems, combining measurements with the coefficient-space Two-Step procedure, and evaluate their performance on various problems including antiderivative operator, heterogeneous Darcy flow, controlled operator, and Navier-Stokes vorticity operators.

items.title: MiGHT-EHR: A Multi-task Graph Transformer for Heterogeneous Temporal Electronic Health Records
items.summary: MiGHT-EHR, a Multi-task Graph Transformer, jointly models heterogeneous clinical entities and temporal interactions in Electronic Health Records (EHRs). It constructs a graph from EHRs with nodes representing entities and edges connecting statistically associated ones. MiGHT-EHR outperforms state-of-the-art methods on average across four tasks: drug recommendation, length-of-stay prediction, mortality, and readmission, particularly showing strong improvements in mortality and readmission predictions.

items.title: SNI-GNN: SmartNIC-Assisted Full-Graph GNN Training with In-Network Embedding Prediction
items.summary: SNI-GNN, a SmartNIC-assisted full-graph GNN training system, reduces communication while preserving accuracy by predicting remote embeddings in-network. It deploys a lightweight linear-trend predictor on SmartNICs to refine cached historical embeddings and achieves 1.3-3.6x end-to-end speedups over BNS-GCN and up to 1.29x over baseline SANCUS, with accuracy loss ≤0.01.

items.title: ED-CSP: Crystal Structure Prediction from Electron Diffraction
items.summary: A machine learning framework called ED-CSP predicts crystal structures from chemical composition, atom count, and multiple detector-plane electron diffraction spot sets. The model achieves a structural match rate of 57.49% MR@5 on 2,075 held-out materials, outperforming PXRDGen, a state-of-the-art crystal structure prediction model conditioned on powder X-ray diffraction.

items.title: Beyond Attention: Signed Integrated Gradients Attribution in a BiomeGPT-Style Microbiome Transformer
items.summary: Signed Integrated Gradients Attribution is used in a BiomeGPT-Style Microbiome Transformer to interpret downstream classification, overcoming limitations of nonnegative attention weights. This approach preserves species identity and isolates the effect of abundance variation, yielding polarity that separates pathogenic from protective microbial signals. Second-order Integrated Hessians are recommended to expose microbiome community interaction rules.

items.title: Toward Reliable Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents: An Empirical Study of Execution Instability
items.summary: Guanghui Min et al. investigate the behavioral effects of recurrent context compression on long-horizon agents, finding that compression can weaken recent interactions' influence, increasing blocked actions and instability across runs. They introduce TRACE, a verifier-guided framework evaluating individual compaction events through paired closed-loop continuations. Initial results show improvements over existing baselines in task performance, multi-run reliability, and context-execution efficiency on AppWorld.

items.title: Mixture of Geodesic Factor Analyzers on Riemannian Homogeneous Spaces
items.summary: This paper introduces Mixtures of Geodesic Factor Analyzers (MGFA) on Riemannian homogeneous spaces, a method that uses geodesic factor models within each mixture component to enable clustering of manifold-valued data with anisotropic subpopulations. MGFA provides greater expressiveness than mixtures of Riemannian radial distributions and establishes root-$n$ consistency for the maximum likelihood estimator. The paper proposes an iterative estimation algorithm and demonstrates its effectiveness on corpus callosum and left hippocampus shape datasets, outperforming competing methods in well-specified regimes while remaining robust under model misspecification.

items.title: Optimized Certainty Equivalent Risk Minimization Using Samples: Algorithms, Convergence Rates, and Applications
items.summary: Optimized Certainty Equivalent (OCE) risk minimization is considered using samples, with applications in portfolio optimization and uncertainty quantification. A characterization links OCE to utility-based shortfall risk (UBSR), enabling the formation of an OCE estimator from a sample-average approximation of UBSR. Mean-squared error bounds are derived for the proposed OCE estimator, and a stochastic gradient algorithm is used to optimize OCE with convergence rates determined by non-asymptotic bounds. Three experiments use this algorithm for portfolio optimization and uncertainty quantification problems.

items.title: The Geometric Mechanics of Contrastive Representation Learning: Alignment Potentials, Entropic Dispersion, and Cross-modal Divergence
items.summary: Researchers developed a measure-theoretic framework to characterize the geometric mechanisms behind contrastive learning, specifically InfoNCE. In the large-batch limit, they proved value and gradient consistency, revealing a geometric bifurcation between unimodal and symmetric multimodal regimes. The intrinsic energy is strictly convex in the unimodal case, while it becomes cross-coupled with a negative symmetric divergence term in the multimodal case.

items.title: Robust Average-Reward Markov Decision Processes: Minimax-Optimal Learning via Plug-in Reductions
items.summary: Distributionally robust Markov decision processes provide a framework for sequential decision making under model uncertainty. The sample complexity necessary and sufficient to learn an ε-optimal robust policy under the average-reward criterion is determined by two parameters: SA (the numbers of states and actions), ε (the tolerance), and σ (the perturbation scale).

items.title: Wasserstein Mahalanobis Distances for Recovering Latent Geometry
items.summary: Researchers Chuxiangbo Wang, Shiying Li, and Caroline Moosmüller introduce a Wasserstein Mahalanobis distance that extends the principle of Mahalanobis distance to probability measures by using optimal transport displacement fields instead of Euclidean displacement vectors. This construction recovers latent geometry from nonlinear observations with properties similar to classical Mahalanobis distance, particularly for Gaussian measures and affine transformations.

items.title: Bootstrap validity in Bayesian semi-parametric models
items.summary: Bayesian semi-parametric models use non-parametric Bayesian methods to estimate a targeted parameter, with a posterior distribution obtained using the Dirichlet process and Bayesian bootstrap. The posterior distribution is asymptotically Normal and concentrates at the true value of the parameter under specific assumptions, including stochastic equicontinuity. Relaxing these assumptions alters the conclusions, and the results are verified through simulation.

items.title: Estimating and Testing Kinks in Panel Data Models
items.summary: A penalised least squares estimator applies adaptive weighted group penalties to the second differences of a coefficient path, and asymptotic theory shows it recovers both the number and locations of kinks with probability approaching one. This method estimates an unknown number of common kink dates in a time-varying coefficient path under fixed effects. The endpoint slopes converge at the usual cubic regime-length rate, while interior slopes are determined by their own and adjacent regime lengths.

items.title: High-dimensional ridgeless least squares interpolation under spiked covariance structures
items.summary: As the sample size $n$ and feature dimension $p$ grow proportionally, the out-of-sample prediction risk of the high-dimensional ridgeless least-squares estimator is governed by the alignment between the regression coefficient $\boldsymbol\beta$ and the spiked eigenspaces of the population covariance matrix. The signal energy distributed along latent spike directions determines whether interpolation leads to benign, tempered, or catastrophic overfitting under minimal moment conditions requiring only finite fourth moments rather than Gaussianity.

items.title: Omni-modal decomposition autoencoders learn full-stack wearable disentangled representations
items.summary: Omni-modal decomposition autoencoders (OmniDecVAEs) learn full-stack wearable disentangled representations, extending DecVAEs by learning modality-conditioned time-frequency latent subspaces through a multi-view self-supervised decomposition loss and a shared asymmetric autoencoder architecture. OmniDecVAEs outperform transformer-based and VAE-based methods in activity and identity recognition, achieving accuracy improvements of 1.01% and 6.75%, respectively. The model synthesizes realistic omni-modal time-frequency data with enhanced reconstructions and distributional similarity between real and synthetic data.

items.title: Convergence of Diffusion Models Under the Manifold Hypothesis in High-Dimensions
items.summary: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) achieve rates independent of the ambient dimension in terms of score learning and sampling complexity under the manifold hypothesis, which states that high-dimensional data often lie on lower-dimensional manifolds. The authors develop a new framework connecting diffusion models to the theory of extrema of Gaussian Processes. This work establishes a connection between the empirical success of DDPMs and the theoretical framework of the manifold hypothesis.
